bridges.statement: The cumulative evidence makes theism more plausible than atheism and supports that God exists.
A beginning universe requires a timeless, immaterial, powerful personal cause.
The life-permitting fine-tuning of the universe is best explained by intelligent design.
Objective moral values require a transcendent foundation in God.
The established historical facts concerning Jesus are best explained by his resurrection.
Immediate experience of God can rationally warrant belief absent defeaters.
The available evidence supplies no sufficient reason to believe that God exists.
Human knowledge is confined to this universe and cannot responsibly identify what, if anything, lies beyond it.
The Big Bang may be an ultimate brute fact rather than an event requiring a divine cause.
Objective moral standards need not depend on divine commands or God’s existence.
The late and limited resurrection records are insufficient for the claimed supernatural conclusion.
Attributes assigned to God, especially goodness, omnipotence, and eternal punishment, create serious incompatibilities.
